chunks: Hadith 2497 — The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said:

"Whoever helps a believing traveler, Allah will relieve seventy-three troubles from him, protect him in this world and the Hereafter from grief and anxiety, and relieve him of his great distress on the Day when people will choke with their breaths."
And in another report: "Where people will be preoccupied with their own breaths."

key_terms.بِأَنْفَاسِهِمْ: with their breaths; indicating the intensity of fear and constriction on that Day
key_terms.كَرْبَهُ ٱلْعَظِيمَ: his tremendous distress, referring to the severe hardship of the Hereafter
key_terms.كُرْبَةً: a distress or hardship from which Allah grants relief
key_terms.مُؤْمِنًا: a believer; here, a faithful person deserving support and care
key_terms.مُسَافِرًا: a traveler; one away from home and in need of assistance
key_terms.ٱلْغَمِّ: sorrow or grief affecting a person inwardly
key_terms.ٱلْهَمِّ: anxiety, worry, or concern about what burdens a person

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for helping a believing traveler in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches the great reward for assisting a believing traveler, presenting such help as a cause for divine relief from many hardships. It links service to fellow believers with protection in this world and salvation from distress in the Hereafter, especially during the terrors of the Day of Judgment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2497 - The Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace and blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family) said:

"Whoever helps a believer who is traveling, Allah (swt) will relieve seventy-three troubles from them, protect them in this world and the Hereafter from sorrow and anxiety, and alleviate their great distress on the Day when people will struggle for breath."
In another narration, it is stated: "On the Day when people will be preoccupied with their own breaths."
